# Trading Brief — 2026-08-03

# Section 3: Horizon Scan — Regulatory & Catalyst Events

_Scan run: 2026-08-03 07:00 CT (12:00 UTC)_

---

## 1. DEA Marijuana Rescheduling — ALJ Post-Hearing Briefs Due

**Event Type:** P0 — Regulatory/Cannabis
**Future Catalyst Date:** August 17, 2026 (post-hearing briefs deadline); ALJ recommendation ~Sept–Oct 2026; DEA final rule ~Q4 2026/Q1 2027
**Time Remaining:** ~2 weeks (briefs), ~8–12 weeks (ALJ recommendation)

**What happened:** The DEA administrative hearing on marijuana rescheduling concluded July 15, 2026 after 11 hearing days. Chief ALJ Derek Julius ordered post-hearing briefs due no later than August 17, 2026. The hearing featured the Government's affirmative case for Schedule III (narrowly built on CSA criteria) versus opposition witnesses (Smart Approaches to Marijuana, TBI, state AGs) who raised harms but struggled to connect them to the legal standard. The Government retains the cleaner statutory path: marijuana meets CAMU under HHS's framework, and opposition testimony on potency/youth/diversion largely described state legalization effects, not rescheduling consequences.

**Why it matters:** This is the closest federal cannabis rescheduling has ever gotten. Schedule III would unlock 280E tax relief (est. $2B+/yr in industry tax savings), institutional investment, and uplisting paths for MSOs. The ALJ briefing milestone on Aug 17 is the next discrete catalyst — the quality of the Government's brief will signal how quickly DEA moves to a final rule. Cannabis MSO valuations are still ~90% below cycle peaks despite the April 2026 interim rule placing state-licensed medical marijuana in Schedule III. Broader rescheduling of all marijuana remains the prize.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| TLRY (~$4.76 pre) | Tilray — largest Canadian LP, US exposure | Sentiment proxy; reacts to every rescheduling headline |
| CGC (~$0.93 pre) | Canopy Growth — Canadian LP with US optionality | Penny stock with extreme beta to cannabis policy |
| SNDL (~$1.21 pre) | SNDL — cannabis retailer/producer | Direct 280E beneficiary if rescheduled |

**Note:** The highest-leverage plays (Ascend Wellness, Verano, Curaleaf, Trulieve) trade OTC / not on Robinhood. TLRY/CGC/SNDL are imperfect proxies with Canadian-heavy revenue.

**What would prove this wrong:** DEA reverses course and keeps marijuana in Schedule I (very unlikely given HHS recommendation + EO pressure). ALJ recommends against rescheduling (possible but Government's statutory case is strong). Litigation stalls final rule for years (moderate risk — opponents built appellate record).

**If this plays out:** Final rule moving marijuana to Schedule III by late 2026 / early 2027. MSOs get 280E relief retroactively, unlocking billions in deferred tax assets. Cannabis sector re-rates 50–200% depending on the name. Cross-listing and institutional flows accelerate.

**Key signals to watch:**
- Aug 17: Post-hearing briefs filed (read Government's brief for confidence level)
- Sept–Oct: ALJ issues recommended ruling
- DEA Administrator's response to ALJ recommendation
- Any Congressional action to short-circuit the process

**Sources:**
- [DEA Marijuana Rescheduling Actions](https://www.dea.gov/marijuana-rescheduling-regulatory-actions) — hearing schedule, interested parties, EO context
- [Vicente LLP: Final Week Analysis](https://vicentellp.com/insights/final-week-dea-marijuana-rescheduling-hearing-ends-opposition-builds-appellate-record-but-leaves-statutory-gaps/) — ALJ briefs due Aug 17, legal analysis of hearing quality
- [Federal Register: Notice of Hearing (91 FR 22777)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/04/28/2026-08177/schedules-of-controlled-substances-rescheduling-of-marijuana) — official procedural record

## 2. Compass Pathways (CMPS) — NDA Rolling Submission for COMP360 Psilocybin

**Event Type:** P1 — Psychedelic Medicine / FDA Drug Approval
**Future Catalyst Date:** Q4 2026 (final NDA submission); PDUFA decision likely late 2026–early 2027 (CNPV could compress review to 1–2 months post-filing)
**Time Remaining:** ~3–6 months

**What happened:** Compass Pathways received FDA approval for a rolling NDA submission and was awarded a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) for COMP360 (synthetic psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression). Both Phase 3 trials hit primary endpoints; 26-week durability data from the second trial confirms rapid and durable response. The rolling submission is underway with final completion targeted for Q4 2026. The CNPV — created under EO 14401 — could shorten FDA review to as little as 1–2 months after filing completion. This is the first psychedelic NDA in US history with a credible near-term approval path.

**Why it matters:** First-mover advantage in what could be a multi-billion-dollar psychedelic medicine market. EO 14401 (April 2026) mandates FDA prioritization, Right to Try access, and $50M+ in ARPA-H funding for psychedelic research. COMP360 has Breakthrough Therapy designation + CNPV + two positive Phase 3 trials. At $11.43 with a ~$1.5B market cap, CMPS is priced for meaningful uncertainty but the regulatory tailwinds are extraordinary. The 52-week range is $3.97–$15.40 — the stock has run but is not at peak.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| CMPS (~$11.43 pre) | Compass Pathways — COMP360 developer | Direct: every NDA milestone is binary for CMPS |
| ATAI (~$7.18 pre) | atai Life Sciences — psychedelic platform | Indirect: sector sentiment, has its own pipeline |
| NNOV (~$31.01 pre) | Innovate Biopharma — adjacent psychedelic/CNS | Sector proxy |

**What would prove this wrong:** FDA issues a Complete Response Letter citing safety concerns (psychiatric adverse events in trials). EO 14401 implementation stalls under political pressure. Psilocybin rescheduling under Sec. 5 of the EO takes years instead of months post-approval.

**If this plays out:** COMP360 becomes the first FDA-approved psychedelic therapy. CMPS re-rates toward pharma revenue multiples ($3–5B+ market cap on TRD indication alone). Pipeline expansion into PTSD (IND accepted Jan 2026), substance use disorder, and other indications. Sector-wide repricing of psychedelic stocks.

**Key signals to watch:**
- NDA submission completion (target Q4 2026 — monitor IR announcements)
- PDUFA date assignment after acceptance
- Any FDA AdComm meeting scheduled for COMP360
- Psilocybin rescheduling timeline under EO 14401 Sec. 5
- HHS/VA data-sharing MOU announcements

**Sources:**
- [Compass IR: Rolling NDA + CNPV](https://ir.compasspathways.com/News--Events-/news/news-details/2026/Compass-Pathways-Announces-FDA-Granted-NDA-Rolling-Review-Request-and-Awarded-Commissioners-National-Priority-Voucher/default.aspx) — rolling review granted, CNPV awarded
- [Compass IR: 6-month Phase 3 data](https://ir.compasspathways.com/News--Events-/news/news-details/2026/Compass-Pathways-Announces-Six-Month-Data-from-Second-Phase-3-Trial-Confirming-Rapid-and-Durable-Profile/default.aspx) — durability confirmed, NDA Q4 2026 target
- [EO 14401 Full Text](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/04/accelerating-medical-treatments-for-serious-mental-illness/) — FDA prioritization, rescheduling mandate, ARPA-H funding

---

## 3. FDA GLP-1 503B Bulks List Exclusion — Final Decision Pending

**Event Type:** P1 — GLP-1 / Compounding Enforcement
**Future Catalyst Date:** Final decision expected late 2026 (comment period closed June 30, 2026)
**Time Remaining:** ~2–4 months

**What happened:** On April 30, 2026, FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide, and liraglutide from the 503B Bulks List, finding no clinical need for outsourcing facilities to compound these drugs. The public comment period closed June 30, 2026. FDA's preliminary finding is that approved GLP-1 products (Wegovy, Ozempic, Mounjaro, Zepbound) and their generic equivalents where applicable are commercially available in sufficient quantities. This would effectively end legal mass compounding of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs by 503B outsourcing facilities.

**Why it matters:** The compounding market for GLP-1s was a multi-hundred-million-dollar gray market. Hims & Hers (HIMS) already pivoted to a Novo Nordisk collaboration, signaling they saw the writing on the wall. A final exclusion locks in the branded GLP-1 franchise for Lilly (LLY) and Novo Nordisk (NVO), removes the compounding overhang, and eliminates the discount competition that was eroding branded pricing. For HIMS, the impact is already largely priced in after their strategic shift, but final confirmation removes residual uncertainty.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| LLY (~$1,168 pre) | Eli Lilly — Mounjaro/Zepbound (tirzepatide) | Positive: removes compounding competition, protects pricing |
| NVO (~$47.36 pre) | Novo Nordisk — Ozempic/Wegovy (semaglutide) | Positive: same logic, plus HIMS partnership revenue |
| HIMS (~$27.67 pre) | Hims & Hers — telehealth, former compounding player | Mixed: already pivoted, but final rule removes overhang |
| TDOC (~$6.79 pre) | Teladoc — telehealth, indirect exposure | Marginal: telehealth compounding sentiment |

**What would prove this wrong:** FDA reverses or delays the exclusion citing ongoing supply concerns (unlikely — shortages resolved since early 2025). Court injunction from compounding lobby (possible but low probability given FDA's clear statutory authority over the bulks list).

**If this plays out:** Branded GLP-1 manufacturers capture full market share with no compounding discount pressure. LLY and NVO see modest upside from protected pricing. HIMS completes its transition to a partnership model with Novo Nordisk. Compounding pharmacies exit the GLP-1 space entirely.

**Key signals to watch:**
- FDA final rule publication in Federal Register
- Any legal challenges from compounding associations (APC, IACP)
- HIMS quarterly earnings for GLP-1 revenue transition commentary
- Lilly/Novo Nordisk pricing data in quarterly results

**Sources:**
- [FDA Press Release: Proposed Exclusion](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-proposes-exclude-semaglutide-tirzepatide-and-liraglutide-503b-bulks-list) — official proposal, rationale
- [Federal Register: 503B Bulks List Notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/01/2026-08552/list-of-bulk-drug-substances-for-which-there-is-a-clinical-need-under-section-503b-of-the-federal) — comment deadline June 30, 2026
- [Lachman Consultants: Analysis](https://www.lachmanconsultants.com/2026/05/preliminary-decision-to-exclude-certain-glp-1-drugs-from-the-503b-bulks-list/) — process analysis, timeline

---

## 4. PCAC Peptide Bulks List Hearing — July 23-24 Completed, Next Session Before Feb 2027

**Event Type:** P2 — Compounding / Peptide Regulation
**Future Catalyst Date:** Next PCAC meeting before end of February 2027; FDA decisions on discussed peptides likely Q4 2026–Q1 2027
**Time Remaining:** ~3–6 months for first wave (BPC-157 etc.); ~6+ months for second wave

**What happened:** The Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee met July 23-24, 2026 to evaluate bulk drug substances for the 503A Bulks List. Day 1 covered BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, and MOTs-C. Day 2 covered Emideltide (DSIP), Semax, and Epitalon. In April 2026, FDA removed 12 peptides from Category 2 (significant safety risk), effectively allowing their compounding. The next PCAC meeting will consider Cathelicidin (LL-37), GHK-Cu, Dihexa acetate, Melanotan II, and PEG-MGF.

**Why it matters:** The peptide compounding market is large and growing (weight loss, anti-aging, performance). FDA's Category 2 removals in April 2026 were a positive surprise for compounders. The current 503A list deliberations will determine which peptides are legal to compound going forward. This is incremental rather than catalytic — no single decision moves a publicly traded company meaningfully, but the aggregate trajectory affects the compounding telehealth ecosystem (HIMS, TDOC indirectly).

**Direct-impact tickers:** No direct pure-play publicly traded exposure. Indirect: HIMS, TDOC.

**Assessment:** P2 — interesting regulatory trajectory but lacks tight ticker coupling. Flagging for monitoring but not actionable for equity positioning.

---

_Sources verified through FDA.gov, DEA.gov, Federal Register, company IR pages, and SerpAPI news search. Quotes as of pre-market 2026-08-03._
